item.title: (Condensed?) French book serif font
item.description:
This is from an 1878 edition of Le tour de France par deux enfants. I’ve had a go at identifying it, but without a definite result. I haven’t seen any font that has a baseline J and the same Q…and then there’s the ?

Maybe this will be obvious to a more practised eye.

item.title: Late 19th Century font
item.description: Does anyone know what the primary font is (heading and body) in the attached ad, and if there is a modern digital version of it? My intuition tells me that if there were, I would see it used, because it really is beautiful. It seems to have been very common back in its day, but I’d never seen it until I recently started looking at old print ads and such.

item.title: English sans-serif of the 19th century
item.description:
Greetings typophiles!

Does anyone know of any sans-serif typefaces of the 19th century from England? It’s rather specific, but hope many typographically-knowledged folk here would know of some.

Cheers all!
